Please leave your feedback about new 'mini.animate' module here. Feel free to either add new comment or positively upvote existing one.

Some things I am interested to find out (obviously, besides bugs):

- Are configuration and function names intuitive enough?
- Are default values of settings convenient for you?
- Is documentation and examples clear enough?

Thanks!

@debugloop, @jotacosta-fb, this should be fixed in latest `main`.

The issue was because during scroll 'mini.animate' tries to be clever of where to put cursor: try on its final position, but resort to top/bottom line if it is out of view (whichever is nearest). So during long scrolls it put cursor on exactly the top/bottom line, which with positive 'scrolloff' lead to additional unaccounted scroll(s). In total it would overshoot scrolling which later is corrected by fully restoring final "true" view. Now it shouldn't do that.

You can tweak `config.cursor.path` to your liking. It takes `destination` as input and should return array of relative points cursor mark to visit. More info [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/17304ee11d0d80ba76c0efd3cf0dbe633278ef11/doc/mini-animate.txt#L201).

I'd give more concrete advice, but I am not sure what you will perceive as "smoother animation for horizontal".
- If you mean jumps for current line, then I simply don't feel like they should be there (too distracting). You can condition output of `path` based on the `destination`, though.
- If you mean horizontal part of any jump then it is an issue with cursor shape dimensions: it has around twice the height relative to width which means animation mark will travel faster horizontally than vertically for the same physical distance. Not sure how to account for that.

It is one of the downsides of scroll animation, yes. The way I ended up compromising about it is by prompting users to make custom mappings for things they want to center. Here is [a documentation](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/06eddfd8d6341e6c4f53ec9ae109a376a566329d/doc/mini-animate.txt#L264-L279) on how to do it. Right now tried it with `<C-d>`/`<C-u>` and it usually results into two scroll animations, which is somewhat expected as first one always results into scrolling. I'll keep in the back of my mind a thought to find a better way to handle this, but I doubt there will be one as I've spent quite some time thinking about it earlier.

Here is a slightly over-engineered helper wrapper for making this kind of mappings:
```lua
local map_scroll_with_center = function(lhs)
  local center_command =
    [[if MiniAnimate ~= nil then MiniAnimate.execute_after('scroll', 'normal! zz') else vim.cmd('normal! zz') end]]

  local rhs = string.format([[<Cmd>lua pcall(vim.cmd, 'normal! %s'); %s<CR>]], lhs, center_command)
  vim.keymap.set('n', lhs, rhs, {})
end

map_scroll_with_center('<C-d>')
map_scroll_with_center('<C-u>')
```

Idea is that during scroll cursor is put at the final position as early as possible in order to reduce visual noise. Agree, this is not ideal...

I just tried the other approach of placing cursor at proportional line and column (weighted combination of start and finish ones based on current step number). It certainly looks better in some cases, but it has certain drawbacks (these are primarily notes to self, feel free to ignore):
- The main one is that it relies on start line being up to date, which is far from ideal (see `L` and `zz` steps in demo). Automated animation relies on tracking certain data (state), which now is done on `WinScrolled` events and some non-frequent ones. To keep it up to date, it should be updated (at least partially) on `CursorMoved`. It seems to be doable but conflicts with the next point.
- It is now misaligned with `cursor` animation, because there is one `CursorMoved` event triggered outside of `WinScrolled`. Not big of a deal with default timings but might be bad if different ones for `cursor` and `scroll` are used.
- Doesn't look good with folded text, because intermediate cursor positions might be inside fold which disrupts proportional movement.

> Any ideas why jumping from top to bottom split causes the cursor to scroll like this:

I seldom encounter this type of "extra scroll after window focus change" behavior, but not that often. But I don't yet use Nightly with `splitkeep=screen`.

I've just tried it and it is reproducible if cursor before focus change was in the screen position taken by the other window. So when you jump back to top screen, this happens:
- Cursor is still positioned on line 75 (as it was before jump), *but* seems to want to be placed on the lowest visible line (60 in your case).
- Resizing animation is happening which blocks other animations. It ends with cursor on line 75.
- Scroll animation is done which puts cursor on line 60.

Currently I am not sure if there is something reasonable can be done inside 'mini.animate' to counter the order of `WinScrolled` events here.

Does this happen often for you? I'll probably look into it if/when more complaints pile up or if I'll see myself distracted by it.

HI, welcome!

It is configurable through `MiniAnimateCursor` highlight group. By default it reverses background and foreground colors, as is usual for cursor highlighting in my experience.

You can customize it as any other highlight group with `:hi MiniAnimateCursor ...`. See `:h :highlight`.

Keep on mind that there might be some highlighting issues in iTerm2. Not sure about specifics, as I've never used it.
